# @goodjin2/dsh-acp-agent
English | 中文
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that connects external coding agents to DSH's native session interface. Su
pports GLM (ZCode), MiniMax, Codex, Claude, Grok, Cursor, and Qoder.
## What it does
**Host side** (loads in the DSH process):
- **ACP agent framework** — transports (stdio, WebSocket), per-agent dialects, frame projection, ter

minal & file sub-protocols
- **GLM (ZCode) model client** — reads the local ZCode coding-plan key, c

alls GLM Coding Plan, streams responses
- **MiniMax model client** — reads/refreshes MiniMax Code cr

edentials, calls managed gateway
- **Preset dispatch** — registers external agents as DSH presets, t

akes over sessions, routes turns, handles model switching
- **Quota endpoints** — host-side GLM/Mini

Max/Codex/Claude/Grok quota routes (credentials never leave the host process)
- **Roster filter** —

hides marked presets from the new-session picker
- **Mermaid asset** — serves the Mermaid rendering

ets from the new-session picker
- **Mermaid asset** — serves the Mermaid rendering runtime on demand
**Browser side** (`./client` entry, auto-loaded by DSH Web via the `dsh.client` declaration):
- **Quota pills** — the GLM/MiniMax/Codex/Claude/Grok pills under the composer, polling the host rou

tes
- **Model visibility panel** — settings section to hide providers and models from the pickers
-

**Model label** — the composer's model chip
- **Switch feedback** — handover notice and switch progr

ess bar when the conversation moves to a new session
- **Turn recovery** — the expand button for int

errupted no-text turns; resend for requests that never entered the transcript
- **ACP process view**

— terminal/file step rendering for external agent turns. It
works standalone and, when `@goodjin2/d

sh-chat-area` is installed, plugs into that
package's `assistant-step` wrapper through the seat
`con
versation.chat.node.acp-segment-renderer` (chat-area owns the declaration).
## MiniMax login: refresh, and what happens when it can't

The MiniMax client borrows the local MiniMax Code login
(`~/.minimax/auth/<buildEnv>/<region>/mcode-

public/auth.json`) and refreshes it through
the same official OAuth core — same credential store, sa

me cross-process lock — so a
refresh here never invalidates the desktop app or the CLI.

When the refresh token itself is dead, retrying is pointless, so the plugin now says
*where to autho
rize* instead of failing quietly:

- `resolveCredential` raises `MiniMaxLoginRequiredError` (`reason: 'missing' | 'expired'`);
- the qu

ota route (`GET /acp-agent/minimax/quota`) answers
`{ ok: false, needsLogin: true, login: { url, use

rCode?, expiresInSec? } }`;
- a model request that cannot authenticate puts the authorization link i

nto the error
it streams into the conversation, so the link is clickable where the failure shows up.

The link comes from the same device-authorization flow the desktop app uses
(`POST /oauth2/device/co

de` → `verification_uri_complete`). The plugin starts one in the
background and waits at most 3 s fo

r the prompt, because while MiniMax Code is running it
holds the auth lock and our login has to queu

e: the first response may carry just the
account origin, and the next poll (30 s later) the complete

link with the user code. Once
the user authorizes, the official core writes the new credential back

to the shared
`auth.json` and the next call simply works. Tokens never enter these payloads, log li

nes
or error strings.
## Where the GLM (ZCode) key comes from

The GLM client reads the coding-plan key from the ZCode desktop app's own files, and it
reads them p

er request — never from a cache, because the app rewrites those files when the
user signs in again o
r switches plans, and a cached key is a key that no longer works.
Two places hold it, the newer one first:

1. `~/.zcode/v2/config.json` — the app's provider configuration. The coding-plan provider
entry carr

ies the key in plain text under `options.apiKey`, right next to the
`options.baseURL` that entry ser

ves. The entry is picked by **the gateway it serves**,
not by its name: the same file also carries t

he start-plan entry, whose value is a
short-lived JWT for a different gateway.
2. `~/.zcode/v2/crede

ntials.json` — the encrypted credential file, entry
`account-provider:coding-plan:…:api-key`. Older

apps wrote the key there. The current
app (3.17.2, checked 2026-11-06) writes that entry no more; th

e key lives only in the
provider configuration.

`ZCODE_DATA_BASE_DIR` moves both files; `ZCODE_ACP_CONFIG_FILE` and
`ZCODE_ACP_CREDENTIALS_FILE` poi

nt at them one by one. When neither place holds a key, the
error names both files and the gateway —
never the key itself.
## When a row doesn't mount: the self-report seam

A module that cannot be imported takes its whole row down with it, and it cannot report that
itself.

So this package ships one leaf module (`./health`, row `acp-agent-health`) that
imports nothing fro
m the package — it still loads and speaks while everything else is broken.
After boot it prints one line naming what is missing and why:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

and serves the same ledger as JSON at `GET /acp-agent/health`:
[该节后续省略]
## 0.3.0 — what moved out

Generic conversation-area UI moved to `@goodjin2/dsh-chat-area`
in 2026-11: the answer card, the con

versation file cards, the Mermaid renderer and
its host route, and the short session-ID bar. This pa

ckage keeps the ACP side and
no longer exports `./mermaid-asset` — if your profile still lists
`@goo

djin2/dsh-acp-agent/mermaid-asset`, replace it with
`@goodjin2/dsh-chat-area/mermaid-asset` (or drop

it; chat-area's own bundle patch
declares it).

Browser layering, when both packages are installed: `assistant-step` renders the
**lowest** priority

entry, so chat-area wraps at `-50` and this package at `-40`
(fallback for acp-agent-only installs)

. Only chat-area declares the seat; a second
declaration throws and is swallowed, which used to make

the result depend on
assembly order.
## Requirements

- DSH ≥ 0.2.1-rc.2
- Node ≥ 22.19 (or ≥ 24)
- For GLM: ZCode desktop app installed and logged in
- F
or MiniMax: MiniMax Code installed and logged in
